entries.core_meaning: وإذا هُمِز المعتلّ المعنى وصار إلى باب من الهلاك والضياع، يقولون: المُوَدَّأة: المهلكة، وهى على لفظ المفعول به. ويقولون: وَدَّأتُ عليه الأرضَ، إذا دفنته. ووَدَّأَ بالقوم: إذا أرداهم.
entries.core_meaning_english: when the weak root letter takes hamza, the sense shifts to destruction/loss: al-muwadda'a = a place of destruction (in passive-participle form); 'wadda'tu 'alayhi al-ard' = I heaped the earth over him, i.e. I buried him; a verb meaning he destroyed the people

variances.meaning: المهلكة، وهى على لفظ المفعول به
variances.meaning_english: a place/cause of destruction, in the form of a passive participle
I heaped the earth over him, i.e. I buried him (I, not the earth, am the subject)

variances.meaning: إذا أرداهم (النص الأصلي يظهر تصحيفاً مذكوراً فى الحاشية 2)
variances.meaning_english: he destroyed/ruined the people

entries.notes: This is a short appended note on hamzated forms of the weak root, not introduced with its own root-bracket heading; footnote (2) flags 'أرادهم' in the original as a scribal corruption (تحريف).

entries.core_meaning: هذه الصفحة ليست مدخل جذر جديد، بل تتمة لكلام سابق عن "اليوم/أيّام" ثم خاتمة عامة لباب «ما زاد على الثلاثة» تشرح أن الياء الزائدة في أواخر الرباعي والخماسي تُعامَل معاملة الهمزة الزائدة، وأن الاعتبار إنما هو بما يجيء بعدها، كما هو الاعتبار في باب الهمزة بما يجيء بعدها.
entries.core_meaning_english: Not a new root entry - continuation of a discussion about 'al-yawm/ayyaam' (day/days), then a closing general note on the chapter of quadriliteral/quintiliteral additions, explaining that a final extra yaa' in four- or five-letter words is treated like the extra hamza (i.e. as an added letter, not a root letter), with the letter following it being what counts - the same principle used in the hamza chapter.

variances.meaning: قال قوم: هو مقلوبٌ كان في اليوم، والأصل في أيّام أيوَام، لكنه أُدغم
variances.meaning_english: Some say 'ayyaam' (days) is a metathesized form; the original was 'aywaam', but the waw was assimilated (idghaam) into the yaa'
variances.citation: نَمَمَ أخو الهيجاء في اليوم اليَمِّ - بيت شعر منسوب لأبي الأخزر الحمّاني، أحاله المحقق في الهامش إلى لسان العرب (مادتي يوم، كرم)

variances.meaning_english: a small creature (jerboa)
a place name
two place names (given together as a pair in the text)
black hides/leathers

entries.notes: Not a fresh root entry - top portion continues a poetic-citation discussion of 'yawm/ayyaam', followed by the closing remarks of the book's chapter on letters added beyond the triliteral root (ما زاد على الثلاثة), then Ibn Faris's own closing colophon praising God and asking God's blessing on the Prophet, and finally editor 'Abd al-Salam Muhammad Harun's postscript noting he began the tahqiq mid-Dhu'l-Qa'dah 1365 and finished the morning of the 1st of Dhu'l-Hijjah 1370, followed by his signature. No bracketed root heading appears on this page, so no new lexical root entry begins here.
